assertions.description: The ATmega32U4 has separate AVCC and VCC supplies. AVCC (pin 24) is on an unnamed floating net (__unnamed_12) with no decoupling capacitor detected. The UCAP pin (pin 6, internal USB regulator output) is on __unnamed_28 with no cap detected. The design also uses a VCC power symbol (separate from +5V) that carries the USB VBUS through the polyfuse F1, but no decoupling capacitors are assigned to VCC rail in the decoupling_analysis output. Only the +5V rail with C4-C7 is reported.

INCORRECT: The schematic has a 2x2 key matrix (COL0/COL1 x ROW0/ROW1) with exactly 4 mechanical key switches (MX1-MX4) and 4 anti-ghosting diodes (D1-D4). The analyzer reports estimated_keys=7 and switches_on_matrix=7. SW1 is a tactile reset button (connected to ~RESET and GND via pull-up R1) and is not part of the key matrix. The matrix is straightforwardly 2 rows x 2 cols = 4 keys.

INCORRECT: The 2x2 matrix has at most 4 keys (2 rows x 2 cols). The analyzer over-counts to 7, likely because SW1 (reset button) and extra LED/LEDGND pins on the MX switch footprint are being mistakenly included in the switch count. estimated_keys should equal 4.

INCORRECT: The ATmega32U4 USB data pins (U1 pin 3=D-, pin 4=D+) are bidirectional and connect via global labels through R3/R2 (22ohm series resistors) to the USB connector. However, the analyzer places U1 D+/D- pins on unnamed nets (__unnamed_18 and __unnamed_26) instead of the named D+ and D- nets, severing the connection. The 'no_driver' ERC warnings on D+ and D- are a symptom of this broken net tracing for global labels in KiCad 5 legacy format. The real circuit is correct.
